title: Serving Runtime Pulse — Sprint 42 Capture
content:
Sprint 42 sync notes (quick capture)

Date: 2027-10-04 to 2027-10-06
Owners: Ava (note-taker), Rory (kernel), Miguel (KV cache), Priya (batching)
Attendees: Ava, Rory, Miguel, Priya, Samir (ops drop-in)

Purpose: short, action-focused record from the mid-sprint pulse check. We tried to keep this lighter than the long retro — capture API-impacting changes, perf regressions, and near-term tasks.

Top-level summary:
- Kernel: landed a small scheduling change to reduce tail latency for short requests; initial dogfood shows median unaffected, p95 down ~4% on lambda workloads. Still investigating a rare stall under heavy cross-tenant mixes.
- KV cache: shadow-cache rollout progressed to 20% of traffic; hit two regressions on very long context (>32k tokens) where prefetch slightly increased memory churn. We've gated shadow for long-context customers until we have an eviction tweak.
- Batching: adaptive micro-batcher prototype is stable in staging; throughput improved for mixed-size requests, but a new fairness bug favors long streams under certain arrival patterns.
- Ops/infra: temporary spike in OOM events on one Dedicated pool after kernel scheduling tweak; mitigations applied (revert + config guard) while we root cause.

Detailed notes
1) Kernel scheduling change (Rory)
- What: switched default scheduling priority threshold to favor short-serving tasks; change is in PR #872.
- Why: long tail-serving requests were crowding small interactive calls in multi-tenant benches.
- Evidence: internal synthetic bench (chat-sim) shows p95 down from 182ms -> 174ms; p99 roughly same.
- Open issue: rare thread stall detected on machines with >96 concurrent worker threads. Hypothesis: lock ordering + rare context switch with GC pause.
- Next steps: Rory to instrument fine-grained thread timeline and add an extra backoff path. Action: Rory -> instrumentation by 2027-10-08 (JIRA RT-2391).

2) KV cache shadow rollout (Miguel)
- Status: 20% traffic, customers with standard context sizes.
- Findings: for large-context sessions (>32k tokens) we saw memory churn spikes after prefetch coalescing enabled. The spike correlates with the new coalescing window increasing buffered prefetch volume.
- Temporary mitigation: disable coalescing for sessions with max_seq > 32k; keep for others.
- Risks: longer contexts will run at slightly higher latency until we refine eviction heuristics.
- Action items: Miguel + Samir to propose eviction policy changes (age+size hybrid) by 2027-10-11; add a metric for "prefetch buffer high-water events".

3) Adaptive micro-batcher (Priya)
- Prototype summary: dynamic window expands/shrinks based on observed arrival entropy. Staging results: throughput up 12% for mixed small/medium request mixes.
- Bug: fairness regression where long-steady streams monopolize batch fill cycles; short bursts starve.
- Root cause hypothesis: batch-assembly logic favors fill-level over time-since-first-arrival; long streams consistently hit fill targets.
- Fix approach: add per-tenant aging credit so requests waiting > X ms get priority in the next cycle.
- Action: Priya to land fix branch and run 48h soak in staging: target 2027-10-09.

4) Incident and infra notes (Samir)
- Incident: after kernel change rollout to a dedicated pool, OOMs increased for one cluster. Reverted the kernel change on that pool and applied a config guard to prevent auto-rollout to that pool until further testing.
- Investigations: memory profiler traces attached to the GH PR; probable cause related to prefetch + scheduling interaction (increased inflight prefetched chunks).
- Ops action: Samir to run a controlled A/B with memory profiler on pool "ded-phi-12" next week.

Cross-cutting decisions and constraints
- No further rollout of the new scheduling change until Rory adds extra instrumentation and we validate on >96-thread machines.
- KV prefetch coalescing remains ON for <=32k contexts, OFF for larger contexts until eviction policy patch is validated.
- Batcher fairness patch is high priority; block merging of adaptive prototype into mainline until fairness soak passes.

Action list (condensed)
- Rory: add thread-timeline instrumentation and backoff path (due 2027-10-08) [JIRA RT-2391].
- Miguel: design eviction policy (age+size hybrid) and metric for prefetch buffer high-water (due 2027-10-11).
- Priya: land micro-batcher fairness fix and run 48h staging soak (due 2027-10-09).
- Samir: schedule ded-phi-12 A/B mem-profiling run and produce initial report (due 2027-10-12).
- Ava: synthesize a short public-facing blurb for Console team outlining the policy for long-context customers (due 2027-10-10).

Questions / open threads
- Is the memory churn in large contexts a runtime allocation pattern that can be changed in the kernels, or do we need a behavioral guard (prefetch limits)? (owners: Rory & Miguel)
- Does the batcher fairness fix need per-tenant config knobs exposed to Dedicated customers? (owner: Priya)

Rapid notes / quick wins
- Add a "prefetch buffer high-water" alert to current SLO paging (Samir) — quick win, low risk.
- Start a short doc for "long-context handling guidelines" for Solutions Eng to send to customers (Ava).

References and links
- GH PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/872 (kernel scheduling change)
- JIRA: RT-2391 (kernel instrumentation)
- Slack thread: #runtime-kv-batching (ongoing discussion)

Appendix (raw outputs from staging runs) — truncated here; full artifacts attached to PR and JIRA.

End of capture.

Notes: keep this doc as a living mid-sprint pulse; will convert to full retro if the fairness/oom threads require longer investigation.
